## Arch Linux Downloads
### Release Info
The image can be burned to a DVD, mounted as an ISO file, or be [directly written to a USB flash drive](https://wiki.archlinux.org/title/USB_flash_installation_medium). It is intended for new installations only; an existing Arch Linux system can always be updated with `pacman -Syu`.
Images for installing Arch can be downloaded via [BitTorrent](https://archlinux.org/download/#bittorrent-download) or right here in your browser from one of the [Arch HTTP(S) mirrors down below](https://archlinux.org/download/#http-downloads).
  * **Current Release:** 2026.08.01
  * **Included Kernel:** 7.1.5
  * **ISO Size:** 1.5 GB
  * [Installation Guide](https://wiki.archlinux.org/title/Installation_guide)
  * **Resources:**
    * [Issue tracker](https://gitlab.archlinux.org/archlinux/archiso/-/issues "Arch Linux Gitlab:Archiso")
    * [Mailing List](https://lists.archlinux.org/mailman3/lists/arch-releng.lists.archlinux.org/ "Arch Linux Release Engineering mailing list")


### Existing Arch Users
If you are an existing Arch user, there is no need to download a new ISO to update your existing system. You may be looking for [an updated mirrorlist](https://archlinux.org/mirrorlist/) instead.
### BitTorrent Download (recommended)
If you can spare the bytes, please leave the client open after your download is finished, so you can seed it back to others.   
**A DHT capable client is required.** A WebSeed capable client is recommended for fastest download speeds.
  * [Magnet link for 2026.08.01 ![](https://archlinux.org/static/magnet.png)](magnet:?xt=urn:btih:ed8507e22addc40fd6fb4f1677bf27fd75967f70&dn=archlinux-2026.08.01-x86_64.iso "Magnet link")
  * [Torrent for 2026.08.01![](https://archlinux.org/static/download.png)](https://archlinux.org/releng/releases/2026.08.01/torrent/ "Download torrent")


### Netboot
If you have a wired connection, you can boot the latest release directly over the network.
  * [Arch Linux Netboot](https://archlinux.org/releng/netboot/ "Arch Linux Netboot")


### Docker image
The official Docker image is available on [Docker Hub](https://hub.docker.com/_/archlinux/). You can run the image with the following command:
`docker run -it archlinux`
### VM images
Official virtual machine images are available for download on our [GitLab instance](https://gitlab.archlinux.org/archlinux/arch-boxes/-/packages), more information is available in the [README](https://gitlab.archlinux.org/archlinux/arch-boxes/).
### WSL images
The official WSL image can be installed with the following command (in a PowerShell prompt from a Windows system with WSL 2 installed):
`wsl --install archlinux`
It is also available for download on [mirrors](https://fastly.mirror.pkgbuild.com/wsl/latest).
More information available in the [Wiki](https://wiki.archlinux.org/title/Install_Arch_Linux_on_WSL).
### HTTP Direct Downloads
In addition to the BitTorrent links above, install images can also be downloaded via HTTP from the [mirror sites listed below](https://archlinux.org/download/#download-mirrors). Please ensure the download image matches the checksum from the `sha256sums.txt` or `b2sums.txt` file linked below.
#### Checksums and signatures
File integrity checksums and PGP signatures for the latest releases can be found below:
  * ISO 
    * [PGP signature](https://archlinux.org/iso/2026.08.01/archlinux-2026.08.01-x86_64.iso.sig "ISO PGP signature")
    * **PGP fingerprint:** [0x54449A5C](https://keyserver.ubuntu.com/pks/lookup?op=vindex&fingerprint=on&exact=on&search=0x3E80CA1A8B89F69CBA57D98A76A5EF9054449A5C "PGP key search for 3E80 CA1A 8B89 F69C BA57  D98A 76A5 EF90 5444 9A5C")
    * **SHA256:** 4e82dced1c4fd3e498b22a853f8db2a4d262d32b97e7e07d97390d9e425ffe5e
    * **BLAKE2b:** f1937fa1bd97175c3b3c658c83849a6e8f482d0431c37622cd228c7733211da43c8c4df16eddd7e842823806117929150aa899d481da0865144b40a206b72937
  * Bootstrap tarball 
    * [PGP signature](https://archlinux.org/iso/2026.08.01/archlinux-bootstrap-2026.08.01-x86_64.tar.zst.sig "Bootstrap tarball PGP signature")
  * [sha256sums.txt](https://archlinux.org/iso/2026.08.01/sha256sums.txt)
  * [b2sums.txt](https://archlinux.org/iso/2026.08.01/b2sums.txt)


##### Download verification
Verify the BLAKE2b checksums as follows: 
```
$ b2sum -c b2sums.txt
```
To verify the PGP signature using Sequoia, first download the release signing key from WKD: 
```
$ sq network wkd search pierre@archlinux.org --output release-key.pgp
```
With this signing key, verify the signature: 
```
$ sq verify --signer-file release-key.pgp --signature-file archlinux-2026.08.01-x86_64.iso.sig archlinux-2026.08.01-x86_64.iso
```
Alternatively, using GnuPG, download the signing key from WKD: 
```
$ gpg --auto-key-locate clear,wkd -v --locate-external-key pierre@archlinux.org
```
Verify the signature: 
```
$ gpg --verify archlinux-2026.08.01-x86_64.iso.sig archlinux-2026.08.01-x86_64.iso
```

### Support
#### Package Requests
There are three types of requests that can be filed in the Package Actions box on the package details page: 
  * _Orphan Request_ : Request a package to be disowned, e.g. when the maintainer is inactive and the package has been flagged out-of-date for a long time.
  * _Deletion Request_ : Request a package to be removed from the Arch User Repository. Please do not use this if a package is broken and can be fixed easily. Instead, contact the maintainer and file orphan request if necessary.
  * _Merge Request_ : Request a package to be merged into another one. Can be used when a package needs to be renamed or replaced by a split package.


If you want to discuss a request, you can use the [aur-requests](https://lists.archlinux.org/mailman3/lists/aur-requests.lists.archlinux.org/) mailing list. However, please do not use that list to file requests. 
#### Submitting Packages
Git over SSH is now used to submit packages to the AUR. See the [Submitting packages](https://wiki.archlinux.org/title/Arch_User_Repository#Submitting_packages) section of the Arch User Repository ArchWiki page for more details.

#### Discussion
General discussion regarding the Arch User Repository (AUR) and Package Maintainer structure takes place on [aur-general](https://lists.archlinux.org/mailman3/lists/aur-general.lists.archlinux.org/). For discussion relating to the development of the AUR web interface, use the [aur-dev](https://lists.archlinux.org/mailman3/lists/aur-dev.lists.archlinux.org/) mailing list. 
#### Bug Reporting
If you find a bug in the AUR web interface, please fill out a bug report on our [bug tracker](https://gitlab.archlinux.org/archlinux/aurweb/-/issues). Use the tracker to report bugs in the AUR web interface **only**. To report packaging bugs contact the maintainer or leave a comment on the appropriate package page.

## A simple, lightweight distribution
You've reached the website for **Arch Linux** , a lightweight and flexible Linux® distribution that tries to Keep It Simple.
Currently we have official packages optimized for the x86-64 architecture. We complement our official package sets with a [ community-operated package repository](https://aur.archlinux.org/ "Arch User Repository \(AUR\)") that grows in size and quality each and every day.
Our strong community is diverse and helpful, and we pride ourselves on the range of skillsets and uses for Arch that stem from it. Please check out our [forums](https://bbs.archlinux.org/ "Arch Forums") and [mailing lists](https://lists.archlinux.org/ "Arch Mailing Lists") to get your feet wet. Also glance through our [wiki](https://wiki.archlinux.org/ "Arch Wiki") if you want to learn more about Arch.

####  [virtualbox-ext-vnc >= 7.2.12-2 requires manual intervention](https://archlinux.org/news/virtualbox-ext-vnc-7212-2-requires-manual-intervention/ "View full article: virtualbox-ext-vnc >= 7.2.12-2 requires manual intervention")
2026-07-21
Previously, we installed its contents in a way that made `pacman` not aware of the files (using `VBoxManage extpack install ...` from an install script). To mitigate issues during upgrade, you can use one of the following methods:
  * Uninstall `virtualbox-ext-vnc` before upgrading the system, then installing it again.
  * Run `VBoxManage extpack uninstall 'VNC'` as root before upgrading the system.
  * Instruct `pacman` once to overwrite the existing files:


`pacman -Syu --overwrite '/usr/lib/virtualbox/ExtensionPacks/VNC/*'`

The Varnish project has [renamed itself to Vinyl Cache](https://vinyl-cache.org/organization/on_vinyl_cache_and_varnish_cache.html#org-vinyl-varnish). We followed this rename with a [new `vinyl-cache` package](https://gitlab.archlinux.org/archlinux/packaging/packages/vinyl-cache). This upgrade results in [breaking changes](https://vinyl-cache.org/docs/9.0/whats-new/upgrading-9.0.html) and users are advised to study these changes and how it affects them before following the replacement. All references to "`varnish`" have been changed to "`vinyl`" in all binaries and directories.
At minimum, users will have to:
  * rename `/etc/varnish` to `/etc/vinyl-cache`
  * rename `/var/lib/varnish` to `/var/lib/vinyl-cache`
  * fix up ownership of files inside `/var/lib/varnish`
  * user `varnish` becomes `vinyl`
  * group `varnish` becomes `vinyl`
  * user `varnishlog` …


####  [kea >= 1:3.0.3-6 update requires manual intervention](https://archlinux.org/news/kea-1303-6-update-requires-manual-intervention/ "View full article: kea >= 1:3.0.3-6 update requires manual intervention")
2026-04-07
The `kea` package has moved all services to run as a dedicated `kea` user (instead of `root`) for improved security. This change requires permission updates to the runtime files created by the `kea` services.
Users upgrading from an existing `kea` installation should therefore run the following commands after the upgrade:
`chown kea: /var/lib/kea/* /var/log/kea/* /run/lock/kea/logger_lockfile`
`systemctl try-restart kea-ctrl-agent.service kea-dhcp{4,6,-ddns}.service`
Accounts that need to interact with `kea` services files (e.g. lease files under `/var/lib/kea`, log files under `/var/log/kea` or configuration files under `/etc/kea`) should be added to the `kea` group.

The Arch Linux [Code of conduct](https://wiki.archlinux.org/title/Code_of_conduct "Code of conduct") governs all Arch projects. 
[ArchWiki](https://wiki.archlinux.org/title/ArchWiki "ArchWiki") strives to be a clear, comprehensive and professional model of documentation. In order to reach that goal we have to organize the job in a rational and functional way: this article tries to explain schematically what are the most important tasks you can give your help to accomplish. 
This is a community effort, but if you take on the task seriously, a formal position as a [wiki maintainer](https://wiki.archlinux.org/title/ArchWiki:Maintenance_Team "ArchWiki:Maintenance Team") may be in order. 
## The 3 fundamental rules
There are 3 simple rules that all contributors, including novices, should try their best to follow as a sign of [respect](https://wiki.archlinux.org/title/Code_of_conduct#respect "Code of conduct") to the other users of the wiki: 
  * [Always properly use the edit summary](https://wiki.archlinux.org/title/ArchWiki:Contributing#Always_properly_use_the_edit_summary)
  * [Do not make complex edits at once](https://wiki.archlinux.org/title/ArchWiki:Contributing#Do_not_make_complex_edits_at_once)
  * [Announce article rewrites in a talk page](https://wiki.archlinux.org/title/ArchWiki:Contributing#Announce_article_rewrites_in_a_talk_page).


All wiki contributors must assume and expect that other users will check their edits sooner or later, and respect their right to do so by making it as quick and easy as possible by following these rules. Those familiar with collaborative software projects will easily understand the analogy between wiki edit summaries and git commit messages, and between wiki edit diffs and git diffs. 
**Warning** Any edits to articles that do not respect these fundamental rules, and as such cannot be comprehended with reasonable effort, may be completely reverted without any other warnings, especially when affecting popular articles.
### Always properly use the edit summary
The [edit summary](https://meta.wikimedia.org/wiki/Help:Edit_summary "meta:Help:Edit summary") is the little text box that is found below the main editing area and just above the _Save changes_ or _Save page_ button. It is very important to always write, in a succinct way, **what** has been done and **why**. Note that [internal wiki links](https://wiki.archlinux.org/title/Help:Editing#Internal_links "Help:Editing") do work in edit summaries, so use them to link to any related discussions or articles; similarly, paste any URLs to relevant edit diffs or external resources, such as forum threads or mailing lists. 
Only in case of [minor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:Minor_edit "wikipedia:Help:Minor edit") edits, e.g. grammar or orthography corrections or the simple rewording of a sentence, the **why** part can be omitted; analogously, starting a new [discussion](https://wiki.archlinux.org/title/Help:Discussion "Help:Discussion") or replying to an existing one does not require to restate the message in the edit summary. 
**Tip**
  * Consider clicking **edit** on a section header: in such case `/* _Section name_ */`gets prefilled in the summary field. It is not a comment syntax—the text between`/*` and `*/` gets turned into a link to a section of the page. Append your edit summary after it.
  * Take a look at the edit summaries in the [Recent Changes](https://wiki.archlinux.org/title/Special:RecentChanges "Special:RecentChanges") to get an idea of what you should write in your summary, but be warned that unfortunately not all users are aware of these guidelines.
  * Use links like [Special:Diff/359881/next](https://wiki.archlinux.org/title/Special:Diff/359881/next "Special:Diff/359881/next") for clickable references to diffs, see [mw:Help:Diff](https://www.mediawiki.org/wiki/Help:Diff "mw:Help:Diff") for syntax details.
  * When you rename a section, mention both `/* _Old section name_ */`and`/*  _New section name_ */`in a summary.


### Do not make complex edits at once
If you want to make an extensive change to a page, be it a normal article or a discussion page, always split your work in several simple edits, for example according to the various logical steps needed to complete it. If in doubt, preview the resulting [diff](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:Diff "wikipedia:Help:Diff") with the _Show changes_ button and wonder if another user would be able to understand it, also considering the edit summary as explained above. Some common operations that generate confusing diffs are: 
  * Moving a section in an article and at the same time editing its content. Solution: move the section unchanged, save, and change its content in a following edit.
  * Reordering several sections of an article at the same time. Solution: move only one section per edit.


**Note** This practice will naturally increase the number of entries in [Special:RecentChanges](https://wiki.archlinux.org/title/Special:RecentChanges "Special:RecentChanges"): do not be worried at all by this, users can easily filter that list by enabling the _Group changes by page in recent changes and watchlist_ setting under _Preferences > Recent changes > Advanced options_.
### Announce article rewrites in a talk page
If you want to radically restructure or rewrite an article or a group of articles, announce and explain your intention in an appropriate talk page first, giving any other interested users some reasonable time to reply and share their view. 
Keep in mind that announcing intended changes does **not** exempt edits from [#Always properly use the edit summary](https://wiki.archlinux.org/title/ArchWiki:Contributing#Always_properly_use_the_edit_summary) and [#Do not make complex edits at once](https://wiki.archlinux.org/title/ArchWiki:Contributing#Do_not_make_complex_edits_at_once). 
## The most important task
In the remainder of this article you will be presented with the various ways you can contribute to the wiki. Among them, however, there is one that you should consider far more important than the others: **add your favorite articles to your watchlist** and protect them against counter-productive edits. 
Every day, ArchWiki receives [several dozens](https://wiki.archlinux.org/title/ArchWiki:Statistics "ArchWiki:Statistics") of edits from many different users: while most of these changes are actual improvements, it only takes one single edit, often made in good faith, to inaccurately alter the meaning of a whole paragraph or a section, or sometimes even unreasonably delete it altogether; if gone unnoticed, this will ruin the valuable work that you and all the other previous editors had done. Unfortunately, this occurs more frequently than you would expect: the official wiki staff does try their best to filter and fix counter-productive edits, but you should never rely completely on them, both because, just like you, they have limited time to spend on the wiki, and also because they are not omniscient, and it is very likely that your knowledge on the topics treated in your favorite articles is greater than theirs. In general, a wiki simply does _not_ work if users only focus on writing new content but then do not care about what happens to their contributions. 
Fortunately, there is a very easy way for you to follow the articles to which you contributed or those that you like the most or are most knowledgeable in: at the top of every article there is a "watch" link, and by following it, that article will be added to [your watchlist](https://wiki.archlinux.org/title/Special:EditWatchlist "Special:EditWatchlist"). You will then be able to follow the changes in [Special:Watchlist](https://wiki.archlinux.org/title/Special:Watchlist "Special:Watchlist"), or by choosing to be notified by email when the watched articles receive updates in the "Email options" field of [Special:Preferences#mw-prefsection-personal-email](https://wiki.archlinux.org/title/Special:Preferences#mw-prefsection-personal-email "Special:Preferences"); the pages you are following will also be highlighted in bold in [Special:RecentChanges](https://wiki.archlinux.org/title/Special:RecentChanges "Special:RecentChanges"). Finally, preferences for the watchlist are found in [Special:Preferences#mw-prefsection-watchlist](https://wiki.archlinux.org/title/Special:Preferences#mw-prefsection-watchlist "Special:Preferences"): among the options you can even choose to automatically start watching the pages that you create or edit. 
If you notice that an article in your watchlist has received an inaccurate edit, or you just do not understand it, you are strongly encouraged to either fix it, if possible, or to start a discussion in the article's [talk page](https://wiki.archlinux.org/title/Help:Discussion "Help:Discussion"), or in the responsible author's talk page. To keep up-to-date, you can configure web-/email notifications for talk topics via [Special:Preferences#mw-prefsection-echo](https://wiki.archlinux.org/title/Special:Preferences#mw-prefsection-echo "Special:Preferences"). 
## Resources
Here is a list of pages that contain information needed for contributing: 
  * [ArchWiki Translation Team](https://wiki.archlinux.org/title/ArchWiki_Translation_Team "ArchWiki Translation Team") has a step-by-step introduction for creating a new translation page. Follow it to translate pages to your own language.
  * [Help:Article naming guidelines](https://wiki.archlinux.org/title/Help:Article_naming_guidelines "Help:Article naming guidelines") discusses effective article naming strategies and considerations to ensure readability and improve navigation of the wiki. Read it before creating a new page.
  * [Help:Category](https://wiki.archlinux.org/title/Help:Category "Help:Category") explains how to set page categories, how to create missing category pages and how to move a page to a different category.
  * [Help:Discussion](https://wiki.archlinux.org/title/Help:Discussion "Help:Discussion") guides you on how to discuss with people in talk pages.
  * [Help:Editing](https://wiki.archlinux.org/title/Help:Editing "Help:Editing") outlines both widely-known MediaWiki markup and ArchWiki-specific guidelines. A must-read for any would-be contributors.
  * [Help:i18n](https://wiki.archlinux.org/title/Help:I18n "Help:I18n") serves as a comprehensive guideline for ArchWiki internationalization and localization.
  * [Help:Procedures](https://wiki.archlinux.org/title/Help:Procedures "Help:Procedures") is a collection of useful check lists for complex operations.
  * [Help:Style](https://wiki.archlinux.org/title/Help:Style "Help:Style") gives guidelines for the standardization of style in ArchWiki articles.


See [Category:Help](https://wiki.archlinux.org/title/Category:Help "Category:Help") for all help articles. 
## Creating
Ensure you understand the philosophy of ArchWiki and think about what others may want to read (see [ArchWiki:Requests](https://wiki.archlinux.org/title/ArchWiki:Requests "ArchWiki:Requests") for ideas). As mentioned, the wiki's scope is quite wide. 
Talk to the [maintainers](https://wiki.archlinux.org/title/ArchWiki:Maintenance_Team "ArchWiki:Maintenance Team") for help coordinating major projects. 
[Help:Editing#Creating pages](https://wiki.archlinux.org/title/Help:Editing#Creating_pages "Help:Editing") covers the steps to create a new article in the main namespace. 
The wiki's subpage feature (article/subpage) is available for your userpage as well. Using it you could create the draft on a blank subpage. Please note that userpage content must not be categorized, but all other features can be used. Once you have finished drafting, you can simply move the subpage to its new name. Please add relevant article status templates (only) after you moved it. The better you describe a status template's reason, the easier it is for users [#Improving](https://wiki.archlinux.org/title/ArchWiki:Contributing#Improving) the wiki to collaborate with you. 
## Improving
Content editing, proofreading, and updating are never-ending tasks on any wiki. If you want to help, just register an account and start performing your magic. 
  * Correct [inaccurate](https://wiki.archlinux.org/title/Category:Pages_or_sections_flagged_with_Template:Accuracy "Category:Pages or sections flagged with Template:Accuracy") or [outdated](https://wiki.archlinux.org/title/Category:Pages_or_sections_flagged_with_Template:Out_of_date "Category:Pages or sections flagged with Template:Out of date") content, [spelling](https://wiki.archlinux.org/title/Help:Style#Spelling "Help:Style"), grammar, language, and [style](https://wiki.archlinux.org/title/Style "Style").
  * Expand [incomplete](https://wiki.archlinux.org/title/Category:Pages_or_sections_flagged_with_Template:Expansion "Category:Pages or sections flagged with Template:Expansion") articles or tidy up [poorly-written](https://wiki.archlinux.org/title/Category:Pages_or_sections_flagged_with_Template:Style "Category:Pages or sections flagged with Template:Style") content.
  * Help fulfilling [requests](https://wiki.archlinux.org/title/Requests "Requests").


### Non-Arch users
Anyone can [register an account](https://wiki.archlinux.org/title/Help:Editing#Creating_an_account "Help:Editing"): non-Arch users are welcome to contribute content that applies to other Linux distibutions or operating systems, as long as they are confident that it also applies to Arch Linux. In particular, articles must be written specifically for Arch users, therefore: 
  * do not add comments peculiar to other Linux distributions or operating systems; for example, a Fedora user contributing to the [systemd](https://wiki.archlinux.org/title/Systemd "Systemd") page would be fine, but mentioning that the newly added content works on Fedora would be edited out as irrelevant;
  * do not replace mentions of Arch-specific conventions, terminology or utilities with alternatives that may apply to a broader range of operating systems.


## Maintaining
  * Add your favorite articles to your watchlist and protect them against counter-productive edits—it is [the most important task](https://wiki.archlinux.org/title/ArchWiki:Contributing#The_most_important_task).
  * Help patrolling the [Recent Changes](https://wiki.archlinux.org/title/Special:RecentChanges "Special:RecentChanges"), reporting and fixing [questionable edits](https://wiki.archlinux.org/title/Questionable_edits "Questionable edits").
  * Flag articles with appropriate [status templates](https://wiki.archlinux.org/title/Help:Template#Status "Help:Template"), like [Template:Out of date](https://wiki.archlinux.org/title/Template:Out_of_date "Template:Out of date"), [Template:Accuracy](https://wiki.archlinux.org/title/Template:Accuracy "Template:Accuracy"), [Template:Remove](https://wiki.archlinux.org/title/Template:Remove "Template:Remove"), [Template:Archive](https://wiki.archlinux.org/title/Template:Archive "Template:Archive"), etc.
  * Participate in discussions in the various talk pages: most users will be interested in following the most recent posts to generic discussions at [this link](https://wiki.archlinux.org/index.php?namespace=1&title=Special%3ARecentChanges). Maintenance-specific posts are instead listed in [[1]](https://wiki.archlinux.org/index.php?title=Special:RecentChanges&namespace=5;11;13;15).


## Organizing
Sorting, categorizing, and moving articles around has become a major task for all wiki maintainers implementing and improving the [category tree](https://wiki.archlinux.org/title/Table_of_contents "Table of contents"). 
  * Reduce and [combine](https://wiki.archlinux.org/title/Category:Pages_or_sections_flagged_with_Template:Merge "Category:Pages or sections flagged with Template:Merge") duplicate pages.
  * Improve wiki [navigation](https://wiki.archlinux.org/title/Table_of_contents "Table of contents").
  * Categorize [uncategorized pages](https://wiki.archlinux.org/title/Special:UncategorizedPages "Special:UncategorizedPages"), [uncategorized categories](https://wiki.archlinux.org/title/Special:UncategorizedCategories "Special:UncategorizedCategories") and [wanted categories](https://wiki.archlinux.org/title/Special:WantedCategories "Special:WantedCategories"). See [Help:Style#Categories](https://wiki.archlinux.org/title/Help:Style#Categories "Help:Style") and [Help:Style#Category pages](https://wiki.archlinux.org/title/Help:Style#Category_pages "Help:Style").
  * Fix [broken](https://wiki.archlinux.org/title/Special:BrokenRedirects "Special:BrokenRedirects") and [double](https://wiki.archlinux.org/title/Special:DoubleRedirects "Special:DoubleRedirects") redirects. Discuss or apply [proposed redirects](https://wiki.archlinux.org/title/Category:Pages_flagged_with_Template:Redirect "Category:Pages flagged with Template:Redirect").
  * See [Special:SpecialPages](https://wiki.archlinux.org/title/Special:SpecialPages "Special:SpecialPages") for other useful cleanup tools.

## Brainstorming
To coordinate contributions with other users in real time, there is an official dedicated [#archlinux-wiki](https://wiki.archlinux.org/title/ArchWiki:IRC "ArchWiki:IRC") IRC channel. If unsure where to begin, or you feel awkward about editing other people's work, you may also contribute by posting ideas and suggestions at [Forum & Wiki discussion](https://bbs.archlinux.org/viewforum.php?id=13) section of the [Arch Linux Forums](https://bbs.archlinux.org/). 
## Back-end maintenance
Use the [Arch Linux GitLab](https://gitlab.archlinux.org/archlinux/archwiki/-/issues) to report bugs and contribute fixes and improvements for the ArchWiki back-end. The MediaWiki configuration is maintained in the [infrastructure repository](https://gitlab.archlinux.org/archlinux/infrastructure/-/blob/master/roles/archwiki/templates/LocalSettings.php.j2). 
## Complaining
If you have any _generic_ negative remarks or complaints about how the wiki is moderated or administered, please leave a message in [ArchWiki talk:Maintenance Team](https://wiki.archlinux.org/title/ArchWiki_talk:Maintenance_Team "ArchWiki talk:Maintenance Team"). Of course it should not be necessary to state that it is indeed possible to complain about something using a civil and respectful tone :) 
All the appropriate places and methods for complaints and comments are outlined in [ArchWiki:Maintenance Team#Who, when and how to contact](https://wiki.archlinux.org/title/ArchWiki:Maintenance_Team#Who,_when_and_how_to_contact "ArchWiki:Maintenance Team"). 
## Getting help
  * If you are in trouble—add a discussion topic on an appropriate page. We are ready to help:)
  * Another option is posting on [Forum & Wiki discussion](https://bbs.archlinux.org/viewforum.php?id=13) or in our [#archlinux-wiki](ircs://irc.libera.chat/archlinux-wiki) [IRC channel](https://wiki.archlinux.org/title/IRC_channel "IRC channel").
  * In case of account problems—contact [ArchWiki Maintenance Team](https://wiki.archlinux.org/title/ArchWiki:Maintenance_Team#Who,_when_and_how_to_contact "ArchWiki:Maintenance Team").

## 2026/06/01 - Seasonal digest
Amidst a record-breaking heat wave across Europe, here is a digest of the notable changes from the last three months: once again, a thanks to all community members who contributed during this period. 
  * Following the upstream change of replacing its monolithic [Wayland compositor](https://wiki.archlinux.org/title/Wayland_compositor "Wayland compositor") by a framework allowing for window managers to be written for it, the existing page about [river](https://wiki.archlinux.org/title/River "River") was moved to [river-classic](https://wiki.archlinux.org/title/River-classic "River-classic"), leaving the old name for the new project.
  * As announced in [the Arch Linux news](https://archlinux.org/news/iptables-now-defaults-to-the-nft-backend/), [iptables-legacy](https://archlinux.org/packages/?name=iptables-legacy) is now deprecated for a compatibility layer over [nftables](https://wiki.archlinux.org/title/Nftables "Nftables"). The [iptables](https://wiki.archlinux.org/title/Iptables "Iptables") page has been updated where needed, the other places linking to it are in the process of being proofread for improvement.
  * Thanks to the packaging changes to [Open Broadcaster Software](https://wiki.archlinux.org/title/Open_Broadcaster_Software "Open Broadcaster Software"), [obs-studio-plugin-browser](https://archlinux.org/packages/?name=obs-studio-plugin-browser) is now listed as available in the [official repositories](https://wiki.archlinux.org/title/Official_repositories "Official repositories").


— [Erus Iluvatar](https://wiki.archlinux.org/title/User:Erus_Iluvatar "User:Erus Iluvatar") ([talk](https://wiki.archlinux.org/title/User_talk:Erus_Iluvatar "User talk:Erus Iluvatar")) 16:16, 1 June 2026 (UTC) 
## 2026/03/01 - Seasonal digest
As we near the end of winter, here is a digest of the notable changes from the last three months: a huge "thank you" to all community members who contributed during this period. 
  * Following NVIDIA's removal of support for the Maxwell, Pascal and Volta architectures in its [latest driver release](https://www.nvidia.com/en-us/drivers/details/259267/) and the [changes in packaging](https://archlinux.org/news/nvidia-590-driver-drops-pascal-support-main-packages-switch-to-open-kernel-modules/) it allowed, the [NVIDIA](https://wiki.archlinux.org/title/NVIDIA "NVIDIA") page and all other pages linking to the now defunct _nvidia_ package were updated.
  * [Graphics processing unit](https://wiki.archlinux.org/title/Graphics_processing_unit "Graphics processing unit") was created as a central page about graphics drivers. The content was previously located on the [Xorg](https://wiki.archlinux.org/title/Xorg "Xorg") page, making it less discoverable for [Wayland](https://wiki.archlinux.org/title/Wayland "Wayland") users.
  * [sudo](https://wiki.archlinux.org/title/Sudo "Sudo") and related pages now promote the use of drop-in configuration files instead of directly editing `/etc/sudoers`.
  * A page for [run0](https://wiki.archlinux.org/title/Run0 "Run0") was created, documenting systemd's [privilege elevation](https://wiki.archlinux.org/title/List_of_applications/Security#Privilege_elevation "List of applications/Security") tool.
  * [Running GUI applications as root](https://wiki.archlinux.org/title/Running_GUI_applications_as_root "Running GUI applications as root") was renamed to [Privilege elevation for graphical applications](https://wiki.archlinux.org/title/Privilege_elevation_for_graphical_applications "Privilege elevation for graphical applications") to improve discoverability, and thoroughly cleaned up in the process.
  * The first step in implementing the [Developer Manual RFC](https://rfc.archlinux.page/0021-create-a-distro-developer-manual/) was taken by moving [DeveloperWiki:Staff Services](https://wiki.archlinux.org/title/Special:PageHistory/DeveloperWiki:Staff_Services "Special:PageHistory/DeveloperWiki:Staff Services") to <https://manual.archlinux.page/>.
  * [Improving performance#Enabling PCIe resizable BAR](https://wiki.archlinux.org/title/Improving_performance#Enabling_PCIe_resizable_BAR "Improving performance") was updated with instructions for [NVIDIA](https://wiki.archlinux.org/title/NVIDIA "NVIDIA") users on enabling [resizable BAR](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PCI_configuration_space#Resizable_BAR "wikipedia:PCI configuration space") as it is disabled by default.
  * [Plasma Login Manager](https://wiki.archlinux.org/title/Plasma_Login_Manager "Plasma Login Manager") went from not having a page to being linked as [Plasma](https://wiki.archlinux.org/title/Plasma "Plasma")'s preferred [display manager](https://wiki.archlinux.org/title/Display_manager "Display manager").
  * All links to [archive.today](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/archive.today "wikipedia:archive.today") and its mirrors were replaced or removed, following [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Requests_for_comment/Archive.is_RFC_5 "wikipedia:Wikipedia:Requests for comment/Archive.is RFC 5")'s example. We will not redirect our readers to a website that hijacks users' computers to run a DDoS attack.

## 2018/12/16 - Official translators
Translating our most important articles, and in some cases many more of them, into languages other than English is a remarkable work that has always been conducted quite a bit in the background in the community, sometimes within a self-organized [Translation Team](https://wiki.archlinux.org/title/ArchWiki_Translation_Team "ArchWiki Translation Team"), other times simply by passionate individual efforts. The Administrators fully support translation work, as long as it is conducted in a way that is compliant with the wiki's general language-agnostic style and editing rules, starting from [Help:i18n](https://wiki.archlinux.org/title/Help:I18n "Help:I18n"). To give it official acknowledgement, a new "translator" [role](https://wiki.archlinux.org/title/ArchWiki:Access_levels_and_roles "ArchWiki:Access levels and roles") has been introduced to thank and symbolically reward users who have made and will make the greatest contributions towards this goal. 
The initial selected translators are (in alphabetical order): [AlonsoLP](https://wiki.archlinux.org/title/User:AlonsoLP "User:AlonsoLP"), [ArchLinuxUser](https://wiki.archlinux.org/title/User:ArchLinuxUser "User:ArchLinuxUser"), [Fengchao](https://wiki.archlinux.org/title/User:Fengchao "User:Fengchao"), [Josephgbr](https://wiki.archlinux.org/title/User:Josephgbr "User:Josephgbr"), [Kusakata](https://wiki.archlinux.org/title/User:Kusakata "User:Kusakata"), [MrReDoX](https://wiki.archlinux.org/title/User:MrReDoX "User:MrReDoX"), [Pedro](https://wiki.archlinux.org/title/User:Pedro "User:Pedro"), [SlavMetal](https://wiki.archlinux.org/title/User:SlavMetal "User:SlavMetal"), [Tuxpain](https://wiki.archlinux.org/title/User:Tuxpain "User:Tuxpain"). Some notable historical, though currently inactive translators have also been awarded the role: [Agent0](https://wiki.archlinux.org/title/User:Agent0 "User:Agent0"), [Blackx](https://wiki.archlinux.org/title/User:Blackx "User:Blackx"), [Hilinus](https://wiki.archlinux.org/title/User:Hilinus "User:Hilinus"), [Kycok](https://wiki.archlinux.org/title/User:Kycok "User:Kycok"), [Maveloth](https://wiki.archlinux.org/title/User:Maveloth "User:Maveloth"), [Skydiver](https://wiki.archlinux.org/title/User:Skydiver "User:Skydiver"), [Umby213](https://wiki.archlinux.org/title/User:Umby213 "User:Umby213"), [Veleno77](https://wiki.archlinux.org/title/User:Veleno77 "User:Veleno77"), [Vladimir Shatalin](https://wiki.archlinux.org/title/User:Vladimir_Shatalin "User:Vladimir Shatalin"). 
It must be noted that the official "translator" role is independent from the membership in a Translation Team: some languages may not have enough users to constitute a team, nonetheless exceptional individual efforts will still be recognized; equally, membership in a Translation Team is not subject to the assignment of the "translator" role: the teams are still completely free and even encouraged to independently invite more users to join, in an effort to better coordinate the translation work; the most active members will eventually be awarded the official role. Novice translators will also hopefully benefit by seeking advice and guidance from the experience accumulated by the official translators. 
Again, thanks to all wiki translators for your help to overcome language barriers to make the ArchWiki available to as many people as possible! 
— [Kynikos](https://wiki.archlinux.org/title/User:Kynikos "User:Kynikos") ([talk](https://wiki.archlinux.org/title/User_talk:Kynikos "User talk:Kynikos")) 15:59, 16 December 2018 (UTC)

## 2016/07/08 - 11 years of ArchWiki
Today the wiki celebrates 11 years of activity, an amazing accomplishment for a project that is kept alive solely by volunteer contributions! As it has always been, there's a lot [going on](https://wiki.archlinux.org/title/Special:RecentChanges "Special:RecentChanges") even right now while you're reading: in particular you should be aware that the [Beginners' guide](https://wiki.archlinux.org/title/Beginners%27_guide "Beginners' guide") and the [Installation guide](https://wiki.archlinux.org/title/Installation_guide "Installation guide") are just about to be unified into a single article, after years of attempts and small shifts towards this goal; if you want to participate, see what's happening in [Talk:Beginners' guide](https://wiki.archlinux.org/title/Talk:Beginners%27_guide "Talk:Beginners' guide"), and possibly also refer to the [mailing-list thread](https://lists.archlinux.org/archives/list/arch-dev-public@lists.archlinux.org/thread/BKJ47PIPFFXI5BLZOQDY6XUOSS4HJ6U6/) or the special wiki birthday [forum thread](https://bbs.archlinux.org/viewtopic.php?id=214373). And don't forget the brand-new [#archlinux-wiki](https://wiki.archlinux.org/title/ArchWiki:IRC "ArchWiki:IRC") channel if you feel more at ease on IRC. 
If you have ever authored an edit in any of our thousands articles, even if only once, even if only to make a small correction, **thank you**!!! The value of this work is the sum of innumerable small contributions from people who don't follow the "somebody else will fix it" philosophy: most people here are not PhD's in Computer Science, we simply share a passion for Arch Linux, the broader FOSS community and pretty much anything related to the digital computing world, therefore if you think this sounds like you but you've never bothered creating an account, take the few seconds needed to [do it now](https://wiki.archlinux.org/title/Special:CreateAccount "Special:CreateAccount"), and start sharing your skills and knowledge, whatever their size is; you will find that the more you [contribute](https://wiki.archlinux.org/title/ArchWiki:Contributing "ArchWiki:Contributing"), the more you will learn and improve yourself too, so it's a win-win choice ;) 
Anyway, Happy Birthday ArchWiki, and everybody keep up the good work!

## 2015/07/08 - ArchWiki turns 10!
Exactly 10 years ago, on July 8th 2005, the ArchWiki was [installed](https://wiki.archlinux.org/title/ArchWiki:About#Early_history "ArchWiki:About") with the MediaWiki engine: since then, more than [20,000](https://wiki.archlinux.org/title/Special:Statistics "Special:Statistics") users created their account and made almost 400,000 edits that evolved the initial blank page into this fantastic documentation resource that innumerable Arch and non-Arch Linux users every day browse from all around the world. 
For the future, several major improvements are already under discussion or planning in various talk pages, with [Help talk:I18n#Language namespace(s) in place of suffixes?](https://wiki.archlinux.org/title/Help_talk:I18n#Language_namespace\(s\)_in_place_of_suffixes? "Help talk:I18n"), [ArchWiki:Requests#Should we remove or archive obsolete articles?](https://wiki.archlinux.org/title/Special:PermanentLink/557180#Should_we_remove_or_archive_obsolete_articles? "Special:PermanentLink/557180") or [ArchWiki talk:Maintenance Team#Reorganization](https://wiki.archlinux.org/title/ArchWiki_talk:Maintenance_Team#Reorganization "ArchWiki talk:Maintenance Team") being only some notable examples. For this anniversary, [ArchWiki:Statistics](https://wiki.archlinux.org/title/ArchWiki:Statistics "ArchWiki:Statistics") has been expanded, and many more ideas have been brought up in its talk page to better show the evolution of the wiki and try to give something back to the most active contributors. 
If you did not make it to get involved in the community of contributors in the past decade, you are very welcome to become one of the first ones of the decade that has just started! The wiki syntax is very easy to learn and use, you can find an introduction in [Help:Editing](https://wiki.archlinux.org/title/Help:Editing "Help:Editing"), and [ArchWiki:Contributing](https://wiki.archlinux.org/title/ArchWiki:Contributing "ArchWiki:Contributing") is there to give you plenty of inspiration about how and where to start. If you have any questions, just ask in the talk page of one of those pages, or any other that suits your specific issue, and the wiki staff, or possibly other proactive users, will try their best to give you a quick and accurate answer. 
Well, Happy Birthday ArchWiki, then! The celebrations will go on until the weekend, as for example the 11th is the anniversary of the first edit: if you want, you can take this chance to make a small gift edit to your favorite article ;) Let's keep working together to make this project grow better and better for the next 10 years and more, thanks everybody! 
— [Kynikos](https://wiki.archlinux.org/title/User:Kynikos "User:Kynikos") ([talk](https://wiki.archlinux.org/title/User_talk:Kynikos "User talk:Kynikos")) 07:17, 8 July 2015 (UTC) 
## 2015/05/24 - Restyled AUR template
[Template:AUR](https://wiki.archlinux.org/title/Template:AUR "Template:AUR") has been restyled with the addition of an "AUR" superscript to make AUR packages look different from official ones: this has the consequence that almost all articles mentioning AUR packages now have a redundant "from the [AUR](https://wiki.archlinux.org/title/AUR "AUR")" wording that needs to be removed. In the same fashion, the "from the [official repositories](https://wiki.archlinux.org/title/Official_repositories "Official repositories")" wording associated to official packages is deprecated. 
Describing how to install a package is still forbidden by [Help:Style#Package management instructions](https://wiki.archlinux.org/title/Help:Style#Package_management_instructions "Help:Style") but, for both official and AUR packages, you can use the "install" word as a link, e.g. `[[Install]]`, to point users to the [centralized package installation instructions](https://wiki.archlinux.org/title/Install "Install"). 
This change was discussed and voted in [Help talk:Style#Pkg and AUR templates: add icon, make them look different](https://wiki.archlinux.org/title/Special:PermanentLink/378380#Pkg_and_AUR_templates:_add_icon.2C_make_them_look_different "Special:PermanentLink/378380").

## 2014/12/22 - Adopt an article
The ingredients of a healthy and successful wiki are both the addition of fresh, up-to-date content (the "attack"), but also protection from counter-productive edits (the "defense"). While "attacking" may be the most entertaining part, please be aware that helping "defend" the ArchWiki is of invaluable importance and fortunately also extremely easy! Just add a bunch of your favorite articles to your _watchlist_ and follow their changes, taking action when necessary: the wiki will receive your love with gratitude :) See [ArchWiki:Contributing#The most important task](https://wiki.archlinux.org/title/ArchWiki:Contributing#The_most_important_task "ArchWiki:Contributing") for a more extensive introduction.

## 2014/10/31 - Unintelligible edits

## 2010/01/14 - Internationalization guidelines
As you may have noticed, many articles have been moving around this past month; especially non-English ones. This was due to a recent discussion on the topic of ArchWiki internationalization. As a result, new guidelines have been drafted and a major transition has begun. 
For more detail, please see the related [forum thread](https://bbs.archlinux.org/viewtopic.php?id=87189) and [Help:i18n](https://wiki.archlinux.org/title/Help:I18n "Help:I18n"). Briefly, the following standards have been set: 
  * Non-English article titles should be of the form **Title in English (Language)** , where "Language" is the localized spelling of the language.
  * Localized titles can and should still be created, but only as redirects to the English-named article.
  * [Template:i18n](https://wiki.archlinux.org/title/Special:PageHistory/Template;i18n "Special:PageHistory/Template;i18n") should be used in place of the old `Template:i18n links start`, `Template:i18n entry`, and `Template:i18n links end` combination.


We hope this does not alienate or inconvenience international users; these changes were made primarily to facilitate wiki maintenance and administration and to simplify inter-language linking. Thanks for all your translations and other contributions thus far, and please continue making ArchWiki the envy of distributions world-wide! 
— [pointone](https://wiki.archlinux.org/title/User:Pointone "User:Pointone") 23:43, 14 January 2010 (EST)

## User statistics
This table shows the 76 users with at least 1000 edits in total, combined with the 246 users who made at least 1 edit in the 30 days between 2026-07-15 and 2026-08-14 (00:00 UTC), for a total of 310 users. 
The meaning of the additional columns is: 
  * **Roles** — a human-readable representation of the most relevant [access levels and roles](https://wiki.archlinux.org/title/ArchWiki:Access_levels_and_roles "ArchWiki:Access levels and roles").
  * **Recent** — the number of edits made in the past 30 days. Includes only normal edits, not special actions such as moving a page.
  * **Total** — the total number of edits made since the registration. Includes only normal edits (including deleted ones), special actions are not counted.
  * **Longest streak** — the length of the longest recorded streak in days. The details for the streak are provided as tooltips.
  * **Current streak** — the length of the last recorded streak in days. The details for the streak are provided as tooltips.
  * **Avg. (total)** — the average of edits per day since the user's registration, calculated as the total number of edits divided by the number of days since the registration date until today.
  * **Avg. (active)** — the _active_ average of edits per day between the user's first and last edits, calculated as the total number of edits divided by the number of days between the user's first and last edits.

From ArchWiki
**Welcome to the[ArchWiki](https://wiki.archlinux.org/title/ArchWiki "ArchWiki"): your source for Arch Linux documentation on the web.**
Visit the [Table of contents](https://wiki.archlinux.org/title/Table_of_contents "Table of contents") for a listing of article categories. 
## The distribution 

[Arch Linux](https://wiki.archlinux.org/title/Arch_Linux "Arch Linux")
    Overview of Arch Linux describing what to expect from an Arch Linux system. 

[Frequently asked questions](https://wiki.archlinux.org/title/Frequently_asked_questions "Frequently asked questions")
    Notable questions and facts about the distribution. 

[Arch compared to other distributions](https://wiki.archlinux.org/title/Arch_compared_to_other_distributions "Arch compared to other distributions")
    Summarizes the similarities and differences between Arch and other distributions. 

[Installation guide](https://wiki.archlinux.org/title/Installation_guide "Installation guide")
    Guide through the process of installing Arch Linux. 

[General recommendations](https://wiki.archlinux.org/title/General_recommendations "General recommendations")
    Annotated index of post-installation tutorials and other popular articles. 

[List of applications](https://wiki.archlinux.org/title/List_of_applications "List of applications")
    Categorized presentation of common official and AUR packages.
## Our community 

[Code of conduct](https://wiki.archlinux.org/title/Code_of_conduct "Code of conduct")
    Guidelines for the Arch community. 

[Getting involved](https://wiki.archlinux.org/title/Getting_involved "Getting involved")
    Describes various ways Archers can contribute to the Arch community. 

[International communities](https://wiki.archlinux.org/title/International_communities "International communities")
    Collection of links to the Arch Linux communities around the world. 

[Arch IRC channels](https://wiki.archlinux.org/title/Arch_IRC_channels "Arch IRC channels")
    Get together with your fellow Archers for a good chat.
## Wiki interaction 

[Help:Reading](https://wiki.archlinux.org/title/Help:Reading "Help:Reading")
    Find clarifications if you struggle to understand instructions in some articles. 

[Help:Browsing](https://wiki.archlinux.org/title/Help:Browsing "Help:Browsing")
    How to search the wiki, find related articles and view the wiki offline. 

[ArchWiki:Contributing](https://wiki.archlinux.org/title/ArchWiki:Contributing "ArchWiki:Contributing")
    The starting point for those willing to contribute to the wiki. 

[Help:Editing](https://wiki.archlinux.org/title/Help:Editing "Help:Editing")
    Tutorial on editing articles and introduction to wiki text syntax.

In evolutionary biology, [cooperation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Co-operation_\(evolution\) "wikipedia:Co-operation \(evolution\)") describes interactions where an individual pays a small cost to yield a larger benefit to one or more others. If this contribution is reciprocated, everyone involved can benefit tremendously. This principle also applies to proactive members of the Arch community wanting to get involved and contribute to their favorite Linux distribution. Their participation benefits not only the community member and their fellow Archers, but all users of [free and open source software](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Free_and_open_source_software "wikipedia:Free and open source software"). 
This article describes how both new and experienced Arch users can contribute to the community. Note that this is not an exhaustive list. Before contributing, please get accustomed with the [Code of conduct](https://wiki.archlinux.org/title/Code_of_conduct "Code of conduct"). 
## Community
### Post on the forums
One of the easiest ways to get involved is participating in the [Arch Linux Forums](https://bbs.archlinux.org/), which allows getting to know the community and help new users. 
### Improve this wiki
[ArchWiki](https://wiki.archlinux.org/title/ArchWiki "ArchWiki") is a collaboratively maintained Arch Linux documentation. All users are encouraged to [contribute](https://wiki.archlinux.org/title/ArchWiki:Contributing "ArchWiki:Contributing"). 
### Join the chatroom
You can help other users solve problems on the [Arch IRC channels](https://wiki.archlinux.org/title/Arch_IRC_channels "Arch IRC channels"). It is of vital importance however, that you read the [channel rules](https://wiki.archlinux.org/title/General_guidelines#IRC "General guidelines") before participating. [Further channels](https://wiki.archlinux.org/title/Arch_IRC_channels#Other_channels "Arch IRC channels") are available for specific topics. 
### Join the mailing lists
Join the discussion on one or more of the public [mailing lists](https://lists.archlinux.org/mailman3/lists/). Make sure to stay on topic as provided in the list description. 
### Artwork
Feel free to share wallpapers, splash screens, color palettes, widgets, themes, etc. with the community on the [art subforum](https://bbs.archlinux.org/viewforum.php?id=47). 
See also [Arch Linux Art](https://archlinux.org/art/) and [Artwork](https://wiki.archlinux.org/title/Artwork "Artwork"). 
## Packages
### Report installed packages
[pkgstats](https://wiki.archlinux.org/title/Pkgstats "Pkgstats") provides a [systemd timer](https://wiki.archlinux.org/title/Systemd_timer "Systemd timer") that sends a list of the packages installed on your system, along with the architecture and the mirrors you use, to the Arch Linux developers in order to help them prioritize their efforts and make the distribution even better. The information is sent anonymously and cannot be used to identify you. You can view the collected data at the [Statistics page](https://pkgstats.archlinux.de/packages). More information is available in [this forum thread](https://bbs.archlinux.org/viewtopic.php?id=105431). 
### Fix and report bugs
Reporting and fixing bugs for Arch packages on [GitLab](https://gitlab.archlinux.org/archlinux/packaging/packages) is one of the possible ways to help the community. 
However, ineffective use can be counter-productive. Please read the [Bug reporting guidelines](https://wiki.archlinux.org/title/Bug_reporting_guidelines "Bug reporting guidelines") and [General guidelines#Packaging merge requests](https://wiki.archlinux.org/title/General_guidelines#Packaging_merge_requests "General guidelines"). 
### Inform about security issues
New vulnerabilities are found all the time. Help the [Arch Security Team](https://wiki.archlinux.org/title/Arch_Security_Team "Arch Security Team") keep track of new vulnerabilities. 
### Help test packages
Packages on the testing repositories need to be tried out and signed off before they are promoted to the main repositories. Help the [Arch Testing Team](https://wiki.archlinux.org/title/Arch_Testing_Team "Arch Testing Team") test new packages. 
### Request features
Request features for Arch packages on [GitLab](https://gitlab.archlinux.org/archlinux/packaging/packages). Before doing so, read [Bug reporting guidelines#Bug or feature?](https://wiki.archlinux.org/title/Bug_reporting_guidelines#Bug_or_feature? "Bug reporting guidelines"), to make sure it is a valid feature request, and [General guidelines#Packaging merge requests](https://wiki.archlinux.org/title/General_guidelines#Packaging_merge_requests "General guidelines"). 
Request features for AUR packages on the corresponding AUR package pages. 
### Create and adopt AUR packages
The [Arch User Repository](https://wiki.archlinux.org/title/Arch_User_Repository "Arch User Repository") contains community-made package scripts, allowing users to easily install software not part of the [official repositories](https://wiki.archlinux.org/title/Official_repositories "Official repositories"). Popular packages get included into the [extra repository](https://wiki.archlinux.org/title/Extra_repository "Extra repository"). 
### Becoming a Package Maintainer
If you want to help maintain the [AUR](https://wiki.archlinux.org/title/AUR "AUR") and packages in the [extra repository](https://wiki.archlinux.org/title/Extra_repository "Extra repository"), you can apply to become a [Package Maintainer](https://wiki.archlinux.org/title/Package_Maintainer "Package Maintainer"). See [Package Maintainers#How do I become a Package Maintainer?](https://wiki.archlinux.org/title/Package_Maintainers#How_do_I_become_a_Package_Maintainer? "Package Maintainers") for details. 
### Hosting a mirror
If you wish to contribute to a worldwide spread [mirror](https://wiki.archlinux.org/title/Mirror "Mirror") network and help deliver package updates to users, you can set up a mirror server and apply by following the [DeveloperWiki:NewMirrors](https://wiki.archlinux.org/title/DeveloperWiki:NewMirrors "DeveloperWiki:NewMirrors") guidelines. 
## Help porting Arch Linux to other architectures
While Arch Linux only supports x86_64 as underlying processor architecture, the acceptance of [RFC0032: Arch Linux Ports](https://rfc.archlinux.page/0032-arch-linux-ports/) has opened the possibility for other architectures to eventually become supported. If this is something you want to help out with, take a look at the [related projects on GitLab](https://gitlab.archlinux.org/archlinux/ports), [Arch Linux Ports](https://ports.archlinux.page/) web page, and join the [#archlinux-ports](ircs://irc.libera.chat/archlinux-ports) IRC channel and the [arch-ports mailing list](https://lists.archlinux.org/mailman3/lists/arch-ports.lists.archlinux.org/) to participate in discussions. 
## Events
There are regular events open to the community for bugfixing, cleanup, and other activities. 
  * [AUR Cleanup Day](https://wiki.archlinux.org/title/AUR_Cleanup_Day "AUR Cleanup Day")
  * [Bug Day](https://wiki.archlinux.org/title/Bug_Day "Bug Day")

## Becoming an Arch Developer
The main motivation for your work on Arch should be helping the whole community, and not simply trying to become an _Arch developer_ by any means. 
Usually, new developers are picked by the existing developers as the workload increases. Sometimes they post a position and you can apply to fill it, but more often, they just invite somebody they know would be good at it and would fit in well with the rest of the team. Having a portfolio of Arch contributions is the best way to make it on the team. 
Here is a list of things that you may do in order to gain some "popularity" towards Arch's developers: 
  * Establish a reputation as being helpful by offering assistance whenever possible.
  * Answer questions on the forum, IRC, and mailing lists.
  * Join the [Package Maintainers](https://wiki.archlinux.org/title/Package_Maintainers "Package Maintainers") to gain packaging experience to show your skills.
  * [Submit packages to the AUR](https://wiki.archlinux.org/title/AUR_submission_guidelines "AUR submission guidelines").
  * Join one of the offshoot projects that may be incorporated into Arch mainstream someday, or start your own.
  * Work on _pacman_ , _makepkg_ or other project (on [GitLab](https://gitlab.archlinux.org/)) and submit patches to the bug tracker.
  * Traverse the [bug tracker](https://gitlab.archlinux.org/groups/archlinux/packaging/-/issues) and fix existing bugs.
  * Find and submit new bugs.
  * Fix wiki errors, add new pages, clean up existing pages and make sure the procedures are up-to-date.
  * Submit translations.

==Getting Started==

Overview

[[Special:MyLanguage/Manjaro|Manjaro Overview]]
Various articles to answer all your questions.
[[Special:MyLanguage/Using Manjaro for Beginners|Using Manjaro]]
New to Manjaro? Start here for an introduction!
[[Special:MyLanguage/Using Manjaro for Windows users|Coming From Windows]]
Go here if you're a Windows user trying Linux or Manjaro!

Online and Support

[[Special:MyLanguage/Manjaro Online|Manjaro Online]]
Our forum, Twitter, Matrix, Reddit, and Facebook accounts.
[https://manjaro.org/enterprise Enterprise Support]
Contact us about various support services for your business.
[https://gitlab.manjaro.org Sources]
Software sources and development.

Get Manjaro

[[Special:MyLanguage/Download Manjaro|Download Manjaro]]
Where to find the latest and greatest Manjaro releases.
[[Special:MyLanguage/Check a Downloaded ISO Image For Errors|Check an ISO Image For Errors]]
Check your Manjaro download for errors in Linux and Windows.
[[Special:MyLanguage/Burn an ISO File|Burn an ISO File]]
Burn Manjaro to CD/DVD or USB stick in Linux and Windows.
[[Special:MyLanguage/Installation Guides|Install Manjaro]]
Installation and partitioning guides for beginners and experienced users.
==Customization and Configuration==

Boot / Startup

[[Special:MyLanguage/BIOS and UEFI|BIOS and UEFI]]
How to enable virtualization, run Manjaro on Windows 10 systems, and more!
[[Special:MyLanguage/Display Managers / Login Screens|Display Managers / Login Screens]]
Install, configure, or even bypass LightDM, GDM, SDDM, LXDM.
[[Special:MyLanguage/Fstab - Use SystemD automount|Fstab - Use SystemD automount]]
SystemD and /etc/fstab options for device mounting.
[[Special:MyLanguage/Make GRUB menu & boot-up/down fonts bigger|Larger GRUB, Boot, and Shutdown Fonts]]
How to increase the size of boot, shutdown, and GRUB menu fonts.
[[Special:MyLanguage/Plymouth|Plymouth boot splash]]
Configure or remove plymouth boot splash.

DEs / WMs

[[Special:MyLanguage/Basic Tips for conky|Conky - Basic Tips]]
Conky can display a lot of useful information on your desktop.
[[Special:MyLanguage/Desktop Environments|Desktop Environments and Window Managers]]
Install popular desktops and apply a range of desktop-specific configurations.
[[Special:MyLanguage/Set all Qt app's to use GTK+ font & theme settings|Set all Qt apps to use GTK+ font & theme settings]]
Ensure QT apps match GTK+ DE/WM theming.
[[Special:MyLanguage/Set all Java apps to use GTK+ font & theme settings|Set all Java apps to use GTK+ font & theme settings]]
Ensure Java apps match GTK+ DE/WM theming.

Software Management

[[Special:MyLanguage/Repositories and Servers|Repositories and Servers]]
Change repositories, find the fastest mirrors, etc.
[[Special:MyLanguage/Pacman|Pacman]]
Instructions for using the '''Pac'''kage '''Man'''ager and more.
[[Special:MyLanguage/Graphical Software Managers|Graphical Software Managers]]
There is a range of user-friendly software managers available.
[[Special:MyLanguage/Arch User Repository|Arch User Repository]]
Learn about and use the AUR.
[[Special:MyLanguage/Flatpak|Flatpak]]
Extend your software library using Flatpaks.
[[Special:MyLanguage/Snap|Snap]]
Install and manage Snaps on Manjaro.
[[Special:MyLanguage/Software Applications|Software Applications]]
A collection of tips and configurations for many applications.

Hardware / MSM

[[Special:MyLanguage/Manjaro Settings Manager|Manjaro Settings Manager]]
MSM can set your Language, User Account, Kernel, Time and Date, Graphics Card Drivers, and more.
[[Special:MyLanguage/Manjaro Hardware Detection|Manjaro Hardware Detection]]
Kernels and Drivers (mhwd).
[[Special:MyLanguage/Configure Graphics Cards|Configure Graphics Cards]]
View, install, remove, or reinstall GPU drivers and much more.
[[Special:MyLanguage/Power Management|Power Management]]
Got the power? No? Then optimize it!
[[Special:MyLanguage/Printing|Printing]]
Enable printing and add printers.
[[Special:MyLanguage/Wacom Tablet And Pen|Wacom Tablet And Pen]]
Configuring tablets and pens.
[[Special:MyLanguage/Manjaro-ARM|Manjaro-ARM]]
Tips specific to ARM systems.

Network / Internet

[[Special:MyLanguage/Internet Browsers|Internet Browsers]]
Security, Customization, and Configuration.
[[Special:MyLanguage/Firewalls and Security|Firewalls and Security]]
Firewalls and Security on Manjaro.
[[Special:MyLanguage/Sync dynamic IP with openDNS service via ddclient|Sync dynamic IP with openDNS service via ddclient]]
Solution for update dynamic IP for openDNS service.
[[Special:MyLanguage/Keyboard and Mouse Sharing|Keyboard and Mouse Sharing]]
Use a mouse and keyboard across multiple machines & operating systems.
[[Special:MyLanguage/Networking|Networking]]
Managing networking.
[[Special:MyLanguage/Using Samba in your File Manager|Using Samba in your File Manager]]
How to set up Samba share in your network.
[[Special:MyLanguage/Sharing files with Python|Sharing files with Python]]
Using Python's built-in network capabilities to share files.
[[Special:MyLanguage/Using autofs (automount) with NFS|Using autofs (automount) with NFS]]
One of the many ways to mount shares.

System / Misc

[[Special:MyLanguage/Manjaro Polkit Rules|Manjaro Polkit Rules]]
The policykit rules implemented by Manjaro.
[[Special:MyLanguage/Add a Storage Partition & Modify your System to Suit|Add a Storage Partition & Modify your System to Suit]]
How to shrink and add a partition and make Manjaro know where & what it is.
[[Special:MyLanguage/Aliases in .bashrc|Aliases in .bashrc]]
Shortcuts for your terminal.
[[Special:MyLanguage/Developer Tools|Developer Tools]]
Set of tools used by Manjaro developers and advanced users.
[[Special:MyLanguage/File Systems|File Systems]]
Information on different file systems, how they work, and how to use them.
[[Special:MyLanguage/Swap|Managing Swap]]
All about swap space.
[[Special:MyLanguage/Limit the size of .log files & the journal|Management of the Systemd Journal & of .log files]]
Manage Systemd's Journal & syslog-ng's /var/log/*log files.
[[Special:MyLanguage/Linux Security|Linux Security]]
Information on root and superuser passwords.
[[Special:MyLanguage/How to mount Windows (NTFS) filesystem due to hibernation|How to mount Windows (NTFS) filesystem due to hibernation]]
Solutions & workarounds for various Windows versions.
[[Special:MyLanguage/Keyboard_Shortcuts|Keyboard Shortcuts]]
Set custom keyboard bindings.
[[Special:MyLanguage/Viewing and editing configuration files|Viewing and editing configuration files]]
How to view and edit files in each Manjaro edition.
==Troubleshooting==

Boot / Startup

[[Special:MyLanguage/Restore the GRUB Bootloader|Restore the GRUB Bootloader]]
Can't boot Manjaro? You may be able to repair rather than reinstall!
[[Special:MyLanguage/Preserve Manjaro Bootloader|Preserve Manjaro Bootloader]]
Prevent Manjaro's GRUB from being overridden.
[[Special:MyLanguage/Kernel Fails to Load (pata_acpi error)|Kernel Fails to Load / "Unable to Find Device" Error]]
Solution for a problem that affects certain computers using JMicron chips.

Software Management

[[Special:MyLanguage/pacman troubleshooting|Common Issues and Pacman Troubleshooting]]
Troubleshooting common issues related to pacman.
[[Special:MyLanguage/Downgrading packages|Downgrade Packages]]
If required, downgrading packages is possible.

Hardware

[[Special:MyLanguage/Did X.server recognise your monitor correctly?|Did X.server recognise your monitor correctly?]]
A quick test in the Terminal.
[[Special:MyLanguage/ALSA|Advanced Linux Sound Architecture (ALSA)]]
Troubleshooting common issues related to ALSA.
[[Special:MyLanguage/Western Digital Green - Drive Fix - Linux|Fix for WD Green Drives]]
Western Digital Green drives have a peculiar problem.
==More==
[//www.mediawiki.org/wiki/Help:Contents User's Guide]
Full user guide on every aspect of Wiki authorship and maintenance.
[[Special:MyLanguage/Basic Submission Rules|Basic Submission Rules]]
How to create an account, and the dos and do-nots for Wiki contributors.
[[Special:MyLanguage/Contributing|Contributing]]
The starting point for those willing to contribute to the wiki.
[https://wiki.manjaro.org/index.php?title=Category:Contents_Page{{#translation:}} Contents]
For a page containing a list of all Wiki guides and tutorials sorted alphabetically.

## Overview
As outlined in the **[Download Manjaro page](https://wiki.manjaro.org/index.php?title=Special:MyLanguage/Download_Manjaro "Special:MyLanguage/Download Manjaro")** , an ISO is not simply a 'drag and drop' or 'copy and paste' duplication of Manjaro's installation files. It is in fact a copy of the raw computer code that makes up the files themselves. This is why it is necessary to use a **software burning application** to 'burn' an ISO file, that is, convert its raw code into the files onto a physical medium such as a DVD or USB flashdrive / datastick in order to use it. Once burned / converted, the files on that medium can then be used to run Manjaro directly without having to install it to your system (referred to as _Live-CD or Live-USB_ mode), and/or install Manjaro on your system. Again however, it will not be necessary to to burn an ISO if you intend on running Manjaro in a virtual machine environment using Oracle's Virtualbox. This is because Virtualbox is able to read ISO files directly as _virtual disks_. 
**note**
* * *
Manjaro will not have full functionality when run in Live-CD mode. For example, you will not be able to save any changes to the system, or install updates or new applications.
### Burning to CD/DVD in Linux
**tip**
* * *
It is strongly recommended to select the slowest speed available when burning to disc in order minimise the possibility of corruption during the burning process.
Several different software burning applications - if not already installed - should be available for installation from your distribution's Software Center / Software Manager / Package Manager / repositories. Popular burners include _XFBurn_ , _K3b_ , and _Brasero_. Which one you may choose is entirely down to personal choice. However, a guide to burning your downloaded Manjaro ISO using Brasero has been provided below: 
[![Brasero.png](https://wiki.manjaro.org/images/thumb/5/56/Brasero.png/375px-Brasero.png)](https://wiki.manjaro.org/index.php?title=File:Brasero.png)
[](https://wiki.manjaro.org/index.php?title=File:Brasero.png "Enlarge")
**1.** Insert a Blank CD/DVD (use a DVD if burning an ISO for anything other than the NET Edition) 
**2.** Start the Brasero software burner 
**3.** Click the **Burn Image - Burn an existing CD/DVD image to disc** button to open the _Image Burning Setup_ window. 
**4.** Click the button beneath the title **Select a disc image to write** to open up your file manager. Locate and double-click the downloaded ISO file to load it. Upon automatically returning to the _Image Burning Setup_ window, note that the ISO file is now listed as the disc image to write. 
**5.** Underneath the title **Select a disc to write to** the blank CD/DVD inserted should already have been automatically listed. Otherwise, click the button to select it manually. 
**6.** Click the **properties** button to open the _properties window_ , and then click the button beneath the title **Burning Speed**. Again, it is strongly recommended to select the slowest speed available. Once selected, click the **Close** button. 
**7.** Click the **Burn** button to start the burning process. If necessary, follow any on-screen instructions provided. 
**8.** In case that Brasero complains about the iso-image not being recognized as iso: switch to XFBurn. This will burn without complaints. 
### Burning to a CD/DVD in Windows
In Windows 7 and later, support for burning an ISO to DVD is built-in. Simply right click on the on .iso file and select "Burn disk image". This will bring up a series of dialogues to walk you through the process. 
For Windows Vista or older versions of Windows you will need to download 3rd party software. Several free software burner applications are available for Windows. One such tool is DeepBurner. The portable version can be downloaded from [here](https://pendriveapps.com/deepburner-portable/). 
### Writing to a USB Stick in Linux
This section describes how to write a Linux ISO file to USB. 
Windows ISO files are notoriously difficult and requires special attention. 
### Using the Terminal
To burn the iso on an usb stick, enter the following command in a terminal : 
user $  sudo dd bs=4M if=/path/to/manjaro.iso of=/dev/sd[drive letter] status=progress oflag=sync COPY TO CLIPBOARD
  

Where [drive letter] is the letter of your removable device. Please note that it is the **device** (e.g. /dev/sdb), and **not** the partition number (e.g. /dev/sdb1). 
To find which drive letter it might be write: 
user $  sudo fdisk -l COPY TO CLIPBOARD
  

  

**Warning**
* * *
Not all ISO are isohybrid ! However you can create isohybrid ISO. If you use very old hardware and rare, may not support isohybrid. Isohybrid created for UEFI should work with "Legacy mode", without support UEFI not will work on UEFI. Before use USB stick check Bios/UEFI settings, USB should start first. If isohybrid not working for you with uefi, try create isohybrid for own use without this option.
  

### How you can check ISO
user $  fdisk -l COPY TO CLIPBOARD
  
    Example:
user $  fdisk -l manjaro-mate-15.12-x86_64.iso 
Disk manjaro-mate-15.12-x86_64.iso: 7,5 GiB, 8006074368 bytes, 15636864 sectors Units: sectors of 1 * 512 = 512 bytes Sector size (logical/physical): 512 bytes / 512 bytes I/O size (minimum/optimal): 512 bytes / 512 bytes Disklabel type: dos 
Disk identifier: 0x00000000 COPY TO CLIPBOARD
  

user $  fdisk -l manjaro-xfce-16.08-x86_64.iso 
Disk manjaro-xfce-16.08-x86_64.iso: 1,5 GiB, 1561657344 bytes, 3050112 sectors Units: sectors of 1 * 512 = 512 bytes Sector size (logical/physical): 512 bytes / 512 bytes I/O size (minimum/optimal): 512 bytes / 512 bytes Disklabel type: dos Disk identifier: 0x06c2dccb . Device Boot Start End Sectors Size Id Type manjaro-xfce-16.08-x86_64.iso1 * 0 3050111 3050112 1,5G 0 Empty 
manjaro-xfce-16.08-x86_64.iso2 224 63711 63488 31M ef EFI (FAT-12/16/32) COPY TO CLIPBOARD
  
    Isohybrid have 2 partitions, you can check also with gparted after burn the iso on an usb stick.
### How create isohybrid
user $  isohybrid -v /path/to/name.iso COPY TO CLIPBOARD
  
    or for UEFI
user $  isohybrid --uefi -v output.iso COPY TO CLIPBOARD
  
    More in <https://wiki.syslinux.org/wiki/index.php?title=Isohybrid>
### Using a Burning Application
#### ImageWriter
ImageWriter should be available for installation from your distribution's Software Center / Software Manager / Package Manager / repositories. Once Imagewriter has been downloaded and installed, ensure that your USB stick is plugged in before starting it. 
A brief guide to writing the Manjaro .ISO image has been provided: 
**1.** Click on the centre icon 
**2.** Navigate to where the ISO image has been saved and select it 
**3.** Ensure that your USB device has been selected from the drop-down menu 
**4.** Click on the **Write** button 
**5.** After the **Write** process has finished, reboot your system 
### Writing to a USB Stick in Windows
#### Using Rufus
[Rufus](https://rufus.ie/en/) is a utility that helps format and create bootable USB flash drives, such as USB keys/pendrives, memory sticks, etc. 
When you use Rufus to write a Manjaro Live ISO to USB you must select DD mode when prompted to use standard or DD mode. 
See its website for more details: <https://rufus.ie/en/>
### Writing to a USB Stick on a Macintosh
As a Unix variant, macOS uses a similar approach to Linux. All commands below should be run in the **Terminal** application. Commands using **sudo** may prompt for your password; this is expected. 
After you've inserted your USB drive, identify it using **diskutil** : 
user $  diskutil list COPY TO CLIPBOARD
  


```
  /dev/disk0 (internal, physical):
     #:                       TYPE NAME                    SIZE       IDENTIFIER
     0:      GUID_partition_scheme                        *1.0 TB     disk0
     1:                        EFI EFI                     209.7 MB   disk0s1
     2:                 Apple_APFS Container disk1         1000.0 GB  disk0s2
  /dev/disk3 (external, physical):
     #:                       TYPE NAME                    SIZE       IDENTIFIER
     0:     FDisk_partition_scheme                        *7.8 GB     disk3
     1:               Windows_NTFS MYUSBDRIVE              7.8 GB     disk3s1

```

Note the identifier **disk3s1** in this example. 
Unmount the drive with the command: 
user $  sudo diskutil unmount /dev/disk3s1 COPY TO CLIPBOARD
  


```
  Volume MYUSBDRIVE on disk3s1 unmounted

```

Now you can use **dd** to write to the raw device: 
user $  sudo dd bs=4M if=Desktop/manjaro-i3-21.2.3-220205-linux515.iso of=/dev/disk3 COPY TO CLIPBOARD
  


```
  787+1 records in
  787+1 records out
  3303161856 bytes transferred in 2470.782563 secs (1336889 bytes/sec)

```

The USB drive can now be removed from the computer and used to boot Manjaro.

## Adding "Special:MyLanguage/" to internal links
Hello! 
I would like to add Special:MyLanguage/ to internal links like this: 

```
[[Special:MyLanguage/pagename|<translate>pagename</translate>]] 

```

like tested on [Test page](https://wiki.manjaro.org/index.php?title=Test_page "Test page"). 
If a link is within the <translate>-tag it should be like that: 

```
<translate>This is a great link: [[<tvar|myvar>Special:MyLanguage/pagename</>|pagename]]
</translate>

```

which will be then displayed for the translater like this: 

```
This is a great link: [[$myvar|pagename]]

```

Is it ok? Opinions? 
Short notes about this are on my [user page](https://wiki.manjaro.org/index.php?title=User:Megavolt "User:Megavolt"). 
--[Megavolt](https://wiki.manjaro.org/index.php?title=User:Megavolt "User:Megavolt") ([talk](https://wiki.manjaro.org/index.php?title=User_talk:Megavolt "User talk:Megavolt")) 02:17, 31 March 2021 (UTC) 
I would appreciate this. This will make translating a lot easier. 
--[Andreas85](https://wiki.manjaro.org/index.php?title=User:Andreas85 "User:Andreas85") ([talk](https://wiki.manjaro.org/index.php?title=User_talk:Andreas85&action=edit&redlink=1 "User talk:Andreas85 \(page does not exist\)")) 06:05, 14 September 2021 (UTC) 
## translations are gone
This page has been restructured. Even if i do support this there is a side to it that i do not like: 
This page formerly was broken into small sections. Each section had to be translated on its own. Maybe this was overdone. But i did translate 95% of it (a few day ago). Now large sections are put together for translation. **All formerly translated text is gone**. 
This also seems not optimal. Sections for translation should be formed around logical pieces of text. So text in one section should be about the **same topic**. 
-- In general, 
  * If you put **small** pieces to translation then the editing of the english page is difficult. **But when changing** some english text or layout, **most** of the translation **will remain**.
  * If you put **large** pieces to translation then the editing of the english page is easy. **But when changing** some english text or layout, **most** of the translation **will be gone**. And this may hit a lot of languages at the same time!
  * Then there is the assisted translation in the wiki. If you translate small pieces of text, the wiki will suggest some similar translations. This is especially good **for headings** , so they stay consistent in translation. But this does only work for small texts like 1 line or 2


So i suggest: 
  * extra translation section for headings
  * combined translation section for the text under this heading
  * extra sections for texts that should not be translated (like commands and results)


--[Andreas85](https://wiki.manjaro.org/index.php?title=User:Andreas85 "User:Andreas85") ([talk](https://wiki.manjaro.org/index.php?title=User_talk:Andreas85&action=edit&redlink=1 "User talk:Andreas85 \(page does not exist\)")) 06:47, 14 September 2021 (UTC)
